title: Microsoft Purview: sensitivity label inheritance for Teams meeting artifacts (GCC, GCC High and DoD)
summary: The briefing accurately separates the government-cloud roadmap target from the preview setting documented on Microsoft Learn. The control path and PowerShell command are supported, and the download restrictions and MP4 encryption requirements retain their documented qualifications.

claims.claim: This is a Microsoft Purview information protection change concerning sensitivity label inheritance for Teams meeting artifacts.
claims.quote: "title": "Microsoft Purview: Information Protection-Sensitivity label inheritance for Teams meeting artifacts"

claims.where: summary; What's changing; Why it matters
claims.claim: Microsoft plans automatic inheritance of the meeting sensitivity label by recordings, transcripts and Loop notes without manual labeling.
claims.quote: Teams meeting artifacts, including recordings, transcripts, and Loop notes, can now be configured to automatically inherit the sensitivity label from the meeting.

claims.claim: The roadmap describes inheritance as configurable rather than an unconditional rollout behavior.
claims.quote: can now be configured to automatically inherit the sensitivity label from the meeting

claims.claim: Roadmap item 581739 is In development.
claims.quote: "status": "In development", "statusKey": "in-development"

claims.where: front matter: targetDate; What's changing; Open questions
claims.claim: The roadmap target is December CY2026, not a committed date within that month.
claims.quote: "targetDate": "December CY2026"

claims.claim: The release phase is General Availability.
claims.quote: "releasePhase": ["General Availability"]

claims.where: title; summary; front matter: clouds; What's changing; Scope
claims.claim: The roadmap item lists GCC, GCC High and DoD.
claims.quote: "clouds": ["GCC", "GCC High", "DoD"]

claims.where: front matter: platforms; What's changing; Scope
claims.claim: The roadmap platform is Web.
claims.quote: "platforms": ["Web"]

claims.claim: The government-cloud roadmap record supplies no preview date.
claims.quote: "previewDate": null

claims.claim: Microsoft lists the same artifact-inheritance feature separately as roadmap item 558686.
claims.quote: 558686: Teams meeting artifacts, including recordings, transcripts, and Loop notes, can now be configured to automatically inherit the sensitivity label from the meeting.

claims.claim: Roadmap item 558686 lists Worldwide (Standard Multi-Tenant).
claims.quote: 558686: "clouds": ["Worldwide (Standard Multi-Tenant)"]

claims.claim: Roadmap item 558686 is Launched.
claims.quote: 558686: "status": "Launched"

claims.claim: Roadmap item 558686 gives June CY2026 as its target.
claims.quote: 558686: "targetDate": "June CY2026"

claims.claim: Roadmap item 558686 gives May CY2026 as its preview date.
claims.quote: 558686: "previewDate": "May CY2026"

claims.claim: Microsoft Learn documents Apply meeting label to artifacts as a sensitivity label publishing policy setting for this inheritance.
claims.quote: Configure label policy settings that are specific just to calendar items, Teams meetings, and chat: ... Apply meeting label to artifacts

claims.claim: Learn marks Apply meeting label to artifacts as in preview.
claims.quote: This setting is in preview and for MP4 files, requires you to enable sensitivity labeling support for MP4.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Data exposure
claims.claim: The setting applies the meeting sensitivity label to recordings and their transcripts, described as .mp4 files.
claims.quote: For Teams meetings, automatically apply the meeting's sensitivity label to recordings and their transcripts (.mp4 files)

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Data exposure
claims.claim: The setting applies the meeting sensitivity label to meeting notes in .loop files.
claims.quote: and to meeting notes (.loop files)

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions; Scope
claims.claim: Inheritance occurs when the artifact is saved to SharePoint or OneDrive.
claims.quote: at the time the artifact is saved to SharePoint or OneDrive.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Data exposure; Governance guidance: After rollout
claims.claim: A later change to the meeting label does not automatically change the inherited artifact label.
claims.quote: If the meeting label changes later, the inherited label doesn't automatically change.

claims.where: What's changing; controls[1].note; Risk assessment: Change & support
claims.claim: MP4 sensitivity labeling support must be enabled or selecting artifact inheritance will not label MP4 files.
claims.quote: If MP4 support isn't enabled, these files aren't labeled when you select this option.

claims.claim: Learn does not state the artifact setting's availability in GCC, GCC High or DoD.
claims.quote: Searched: "Apply meeting label to artifacts" "GCC"; read sensitivity-labels-meetings and the returned government-labeling excerpts. No artifact-setting availability statement for GCC, GCC High or DoD was found.

claims.where: front matter: defaultState; Why it matters; Open questions; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Microsoft has not stated the artifact setting's initial default, so defaultState is unknown.
claims.quote: Searched: "Apply meeting label to artifacts" "default"; read roadmap 581739, sensitivity-labels-meetings and create-sensitivity-labels. They describe configuration but do not state whether the new option is initially selected.

claims.claim: Sensitivity labels applying encryption to MP4 files must use Assign permissions now rather than user-defined permissions.
claims.quote: Sensitivity labels that apply encryption must be configured with the Assign permissions now option, rather than user-defined permissions.

claims.where: Why it matters; Risk assessment: Security & identity; Governance guidance; rationale: impact
claims.claim: A recording and transcript carrying a label that applies encryption cannot be downloaded.
claims.quote: However, if a recording and transcript has a label that applies encryption, you can't download them.

claims.claim: Recordings and transcripts can be downloaded if their label does not apply encryption.
claims.quote: You can download them if the label doesn't apply encryption

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity; rationale: impact
claims.claim: A downloaded unencrypted file in this scenario does not retain labeling information.
claims.quote: but a downloaded file in this case doesn't retain the labeling information.

claims.claim: Recordings respect the access permissions and usage rights in the label encryption settings.
claims.quote: Recordings respect any access permissions and usage rights from label encryption settings

claims.where: Risk assessment: Change & support; Governance guidance: At rollout
claims.claim: Labeled encrypted recordings support playback in the browser despite the download restriction.
claims.quote: can be played directly in a web browser and supported experiences such as SharePoint, Teams, or Clipchamp.

claims.claim: These files can be manually relabeled in SharePoint or OneDrive using the file's Details pane.
claims.quote: You can, if required, manually relabel these files in SharePoint or OneDrive, by using the file's Details pane.

claims.claim: Relabeling by an owner or administrator remains subject to appropriate permissions to change an encrypting label.
claims.quote: you must have the appropriate permissions to change a sensitivity label that applies encryption, which is always the case for the meeting owner.

claims.claim: No approval step is documented for applying the inherited label.
claims.quote: Searched: "meeting label" "artifacts" "approval"; read sensitivity-labels-meetings. The documented behavior is automatic application at save time; no approval step is described.

claims.claim: A label configured to protect meetings must include Files & other data assets, Emails and Meetings scopes.
claims.quote: Files & other data assets; Emails; Meetings. All three options are needed because of their interdependency.

claims.claim: The label must be published to meeting organizers and participants.
claims.quote: Make sure the label is published to meeting organizers and participants.

claims.claim: Enforcing label meeting options requires a supported Teams client, with minimum versions documented on Learn.
claims.quote: To apply a sensitivity label to meeting invites using Teams, enforce meeting options and chat, and display and change sensitivity labels in Teams non-channel meetings, users must use Teams on the web with Edge or Chrome, or one of the following Teams clients

claims.claim: Configured label meeting options cannot be enforced for users whose Teams clients do not meet the requirements.
claims.quote: If meeting participants or organizers don't use a Teams client that meets these requirements, the configured label meeting options can't be enforced for these users.

claims.claim: The Learn meetings-labeling page lists no price or meter for this setting.
claims.quote: Searched: "Apply meeting label to artifacts" price meter cost; read sensitivity-labels-meetings and the Purview service description sensitivity-labeling section. No price or meter for the artifact option was found.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; rationale: cost
claims.claim: The Purview service description says sensitivity labeling, including automatic or policy-based labeling, requires Microsoft 365 E5 or Microsoft 365 Information Protection and Governance.
claims.quote: Sensitivity labeling, including automatic or policy-based labeling, requires a Microsoft 365 E5 license or Microsoft 365 Information Protection and Governance (IPG).

claims.claim: The service description lists manual sensitivity labeling for Teams online meetings under Microsoft 365 E5/A5/G5 plus Teams Premium.
claims.quote: Microsoft 365 E5/A5/G5 + Teams Premium ... Manual Sensitivity Labeling for Teams online meetings | Included

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; rationale: cost
claims.claim: Some options on the meetings-labeling page cannot be configured without a Teams Premium license in the tenant.
claims.quote: You won't be able to configure all the options referenced on this page if a Teams Premium license isn't found for your tenant.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; Open questions; rationale: cost
claims.claim: No license statement specific to the artifact inheritance setting was found beyond the published surrounding labeling requirements.
claims.quote: Searched: "Apply meeting label to artifacts" "license" and "meeting artifacts" "label" "licensing"; read sensitivity-labels-meetings and the Purview service description's labeling tables. Neither names a license specifically for the artifact inheritance option.

claims.claim: The mixed licensing model reflects the documented labeling entitlement and Teams Premium requirements, without asserting a specific entitlement for artifact inheritance.
claims.quote: Sensitivity labeling, including automatic or policy-based labeling, requires a Microsoft 365 E5 license or Microsoft 365 Information Protection and Governance (IPG). ... Microsoft 365 E5/A5/G5 + Teams Premium

claims.claim: The setting is reached in Microsoft Purview portal through Solutions > Information Protection > Publishing policies > Publish label > Apply meeting label to artifacts.
claims.quote: Sign in to the Microsoft Purview portal > Solutions > Information Protection > Publishing policies. ... select Publish label to start the Create policy configuration.

claims.claim: No PowerShell or API operation for the artifact inheritance option is documented in the references searched.
claims.quote: Searched: "Set-LabelPolicy" "artifacts"; "Apply meeting label to artifacts" "PowerShell" "AdvancedSettings". Read Set-LabelPolicy advanced settings, meetings configuration and client-advanced-settings search excerpts; no artifact-setting operation was documented.

claims.claim: An existing publishing policy can be edited by selecting Edit Policy.
claims.quote: To edit an existing label policy, select it, and then select the Edit Policy button from the flyout pane

claims.where: controls[0].scope; Governance controls; Governance guidance: At rollout
claims.claim: The label policy settings are scoped to the users and groups selected for publication.
claims.quote: As part of the label policy, you select users and groups to have sensitivity labels and label policy settings.

claims.where: controls[1].api; Governance controls table; Governance guidance: Before rollout
claims.claim: SharePoint Online PowerShell command Set-SPOTenant -EnableSensitivityLabelForVideoFiles $true enables sensitivity label support for MP4 videos.
claims.quote: To turn on support for MP4 video files, use the Set-SPOTenant cmdlet with the EnableSensitivityLabelForVideoFiles parameter: Set-SPOTenant -EnableSensitivityLabelForVideoFiles $true

claims.claim: No admin UI for enabling the MP4-specific sensitivity label support is documented in the searched material.
claims.quote: Searched: "EnableSensitivityLabelForVideoFiles" "admin" portal; read sensitivity-labels-sharepoint-onedrive-files and video-purview excerpts. MP4 enablement uses PowerShell; the portal Turn on now instructions concern general labeling support, not this MP4 switch.

claims.claim: EnableSensitivityLabelForVideoFiles also controls sensitivity label behavior for Clipchamp projects.
claims.quote: The same setting also controls sensitivity label behavior for Clipchamp projects.

claims.claim: The SharePoint setting applies across the tenant, or the connected geo-location in a Multi-Geo organization.
claims.quote: The setting applies across the tenant, or the connected geo-location in a Multi-Geo organization; review its effect before changing it.

claims.where: Governance guidance: Before rollout; Governance controls
claims.claim: Multi-Geo tenants must connect to each geo-location and run the MP4 enablement command separately.
claims.quote: For Microsoft 365 Multi-Geo, you must connect to each of your geo-locations and run the command separately.

claims.claim: Set-LabelPolicy's documented advanced settings include mandatory and default labels for meetings.
claims.quote: TeamworkMandatory: Outlook and Teams apps that support this setting can enable or disable mandatory labeling for meetings. ... teamworkdefaultlabelid: Outlook and Teams apps that support this setting apply a default label, or no label for meetings.

claims.claim: Learn's description of the artifact setting does not itself name a required administrator role.
claims.quote: Searched: "Apply meeting label to artifacts" administrator role permissions; read sensitivity-labels-meetings. Its artifact-setting description names relabeling permissions and the meeting owner but no administrator role for configuring the option.

claims.claim: Microsoft advises allowing 24 hours for label and label policy changes to propagate before troubleshooting.
claims.quote: For labels and label policy settings, allow 24 hours for the changes to propagate through the services. ... it's a good idea to wait this 24-hour time period before you spend time troubleshooting labels and label policies for recent changes.

controlChecks.governs: Whether a label policy applies the meeting's label to recordings, transcripts and Loop notes
Whether .mp4 meeting recordings can carry a sensitivity label
